lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to Stage 3! Look at this tall tower. It's the Tower of Messages. Messages fly from this tower every day. Say it with me. Messages fly from this tower every day. Great! Look at the birds. Birds carry letters to people far away. In this world, we will learn how to talk on the phone, how to make video calls, and how to write emails. We will connect with people who are far away. From now on, I will speak only English. （これからは えいごだけ。だいじょうぶ！） Don't worry. Listen carefully, look at the pictures, and guess. You can do it! Here is a note on the tower door. Let's read it together. "Welcome, travelers! This is the Tower of Messages. Every morning, our birds carry letters to many towns. Please come in and look around. You can make phone calls on the second floor." Now, phonics. Today's word part is d i s. Like, dislike. Agree, disagree. Appear, disappear. Dis means not, or the opposite. Oh, look! The letter just disappeared! Where did it go? Ha ha, a bird took it. Let's go inside!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, we are in the phone room of the tower. Let's make our first phone call. On the phone, we don't say, I'm Haru. We say, This is Haru. Listen. Hello, this is Haru. May I speak to Riko? Say it with me. Hello, this is Haru. May I speak to Riko? Wonderful! May I speak to is a polite way to ask for someone. Then the other person says, Yes. Just a moment, please. Or, if Riko answers, she says, This is Riko speaking. Let's read a short phone call together. Ring, ring. "Hello?" "Hello, this is Kiko. May I speak to Birimo?" "This is Birimo speaking! Hi, Kiko!" "Hi, Birimo! Are you busy?" "No, I'm just eating a banana." Ha ha. Remember, on the phone, people can't see your face. So speak slowly and clearly, and use a friendly voice. Now, phonics. Connect, disconnect. Honest, dishonest. Obey, disobey. D i s makes the opposite. If you push this red button, you disconnect the call. Don't push it yet! Now, let's call a friend.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, Kiko is working at the front desk of the tower. The phone rings a lot! When someone calls and asks for a person, we say, Hold on, please. I'll get her. Say it with me. Hold on, please. I'll get her. Excellent! Hold on means wait a little. （hold on ＝ ちょっと まってね） For a boy, say, I'll get him. If you don't know the caller, ask politely. Who's calling, please? When you come back, say, Thank you for waiting. Let's read the front desk rules. "Front Desk Rules. One. Answer the phone with a smile. Two. Ask, Who's calling, please? Three. Say, Hold on, please. Then get the person quickly. Four. Keep the desk tidy." A tidy desk helps you find the message notes quickly. Oh, look at this desk. Papers everywhere! It's in disorder. Let's tidy it up. Now, phonics. Order, disorder. Comfort, discomfort. Like, dislike. I dislike a messy desk. Do you? Now it's your turn at the front desk. Ring, ring!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Ring, ring! Kiko picks up the phone. "Hello, may I speak to Tom?" Tom? There's no one named Tom in the tower. It's a wrong number! What should we say? We say it politely. I'm sorry. I think you have the wrong number. Say it with me. I'm sorry. I think you have the wrong number. Very good! Why do we say I think? It sounds softer and kinder. The caller may say, Oh, sorry to bother you. And we can say, That's okay. Goodbye. Let's read a wrong number call. "Hello, is this Sunny Bakery?" "No, this is the Tower of Messages. I think you have the wrong number." "Oh, sorry to bother you!" "That's okay. Have a nice day!" One more important thing. If a stranger asks your name or address on the phone, don't tell them. Just say, Please wait, and get an adult. Now, phonics. Agree, disagree. Connect, disconnect. And remember u n from World 18. Happy, unhappy. Lock, unlock. Both make the opposite. Let's practice!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! This is our first review day in Stage 3. Today, let's invite a friend on the phone. When you call a good friend, you can say, Hi, it's Kiko. It's more friendly than This is Kiko. Then ask, Are you free on Saturday? Say it with me. Hi, it's Kiko. Are you free on Saturday? Great job! Then invite your friend. Do you want to go to the park with me? Your friend can say, Sounds great! What time? Or, I'd love to, but I'm busy. Let's read a phone call between Riko and Haru. "Hi, Haru. It's Riko." "Hi, Riko! What's up?" "Are you free on Saturday?" "Yes, I am. Why?" "Do you want to watch the birds with me? They fly at ten in the morning." "Sounds great! See you at ten!" Remember, friends say Hi, it's Riko. For a polite call, say This is Riko. Now, phonics review. Dislike. Disappear. Dishonest. Disobey. Don't be dishonest, and don't disappear on Saturday! Ha ha. Now, call your friend!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! I went back to Festival Island for a few days. I'm helping my aunt. But we can still talk. Let's make a video call! At the start of a video call, check the sound. Ask, Can you hear me? Say it with me. Can you hear me? If you can hear well, say, Yes, loud and clear. That means the sound is good. You can also ask, Can you see me? Sometimes the camera doesn't work. Then you say, I can hear you, but I can't see you. Let's read the chat message I sent you this morning. "Hi, everyone! Let's have a video call at four o'clock today. Please sit near the window. The internet is better there. I can't wait to see your faces! From Ms. Emma" Here are some video call manners. Look at the camera. Speak clearly. Wait for your turn. Now, phonics. Today's word part is m i s. It means wrong. Take, mistake. Spell, misspell. Hear, mishear. On a video call, people sometimes mishear words. That's okay. Just ask again. Ready? Let's start the call!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Video calls are fun, but sometimes there are problems. Look. Birimo is talking, but we can't hear anything. Why? Look at the microphone button. It has a line on it. Birimo is on mute. （mute ＝ おとが でない） We can help him. Say, You're on mute. Click the microphone. Say it with me. You're on mute. Click the microphone. Nice! If you can't see your friend, say, Can you turn on your camera? And when it works, say, Now I can hear you! Here is a video call checklist. Read it with me. "Before the call: Turn on your camera. Check your microphone. During the call: Mute yourself when it's noisy. Click the microphone again when you want to talk. Look at the camera, not at the floor." Good! Being on mute is not a big mistake. It happens to everyone, even teachers! Now, phonics. Understand, misunderstand. Place, misplace. Take, mistake. Oh no, I misplaced my glasses. Where are they? Oh, they're on my head! Ha ha. Let's practice helping a friend on mute.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, the internet in the tower is slow because of the strong wind. Look at my face on the screen. It's not moving! The screen froze. Froze is the past of freeze. When the screen freezes, you miss some words. So you say, The screen froze. Can you say that again? Say it with me. The screen froze. Can you say that again? Super! Sometimes the voice comes and goes. Then say, Sorry, you're breaking up. If it doesn't get better, say, Let me call you back. Then hang up and call again. Let's read a chat during a video call. "Riko: Ms. Emma, the screen froze. Can you say that again? Ms. Emma: Sure. I said, The festival was wonderful. Riko: Thanks! Now I can hear you clearly." Asking again is good. It's not rude. Good listeners ask again! Now, phonics. P r e means before. View, preview. School, preschool. Heat, preheat. Before a video call, you can preview your camera. Then you can check your face and your room. Let's practice!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! I'm still on Festival Island, so let's have a video call again. Today, let's show our rooms on the video call. You can say, Let me show you my room. Say it with me. Let me show you my room. Great! Let me means I will do it for you. Then move your camera slowly and explain. On the left, there's a big bookshelf. On the right, there's a window. This is my favorite poster. Let's read what Haru said on his video call. "Let me show you my room in the tower. On the left, there's a bed. Next to the bed, there's a small desk. On the desk, there's a lamp shaped like a bird. In the corner, there's a big map. This is my favorite thing. It's a map of all the worlds!" Wonderful! One more tip. Before you show your room on a video call, check the camera. Don't show letters with your address, or family photos, to people you don't know. Now, phonics. Mistake. Misspell. Preview. Pretest. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The world is big. When it's morning in one country, it's night in another country. This is called the time difference. Today, Birimo will play a friend in a faraway country. When you call a friend far away, ask, What time is it there? Say it with me. What time is it there? Excellent! Your friend may say, It's nine at night. It's dark here. And you can say, Really? It's nine in the morning here. Let's read a message from a faraway friend. "Hi! It's eight in the evening here. I just finished dinner. What time is it there? Is it morning? Let's have a video call this weekend. Saturday morning for you is Friday night for me!" Isn't that interesting? Before you call someone far away, check the time. Don't call when your friend is sleeping! Now, phonics review. Dislike. Mishear. Prepay. Misunderstand. D i s, opposite. M i s, wrong. P r e, before. On a long-distance call, it's easy to mishear. So speak clearly. Great job this week!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! I'm back from the island! Thank you for all the video calls. Today, we are working at the Message Center on the fifth floor. Many people call here. Sometimes the person they want is not here. Then we say, She's out right now. Can I take a message? Say it with me. She's out right now. Can I take a message? Perfect! Out means not at home, or not here. Take a message means write down the words for someone. The caller says, Yes, please, and gives the message. You write a note and say, Sure. I'll tell her. Look at this message note. Let's read it. "Message for: Riko. From: Kiko. Time: 3:15. Message: The bird show starts at five. Please come to the top floor." A good message note has four things: who it's for, who it's from, the time, and the message. Now, phonics. T e l e means far. Telephone. Phone means sound, so a telephone carries sound from far away. Telescope. You can see far stars with it. Television. You can see pictures from far away. Let's take messages!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Yesterday, we took messages. Today, let's ask someone to give a message. When the person you want is out, you can say, Could you tell her to call me back? Say it with me. Could you tell her to call me back? Very good! Could you is a polite way to ask a favor. Tell her to call me back means please ask her to call me later. For a boy, say tell him. You can also say, Could you tell him the party is at six? The other person says, No problem. I'll tell her. Let's read a phone call. "Hello, this is Riko. May I speak to Ms. Emma?" "Sorry, she's out right now." "Oh, okay. Could you tell her to call me back? I have a question about the bird show." "No problem. I'll tell her." "Thank you. Bye!" Remember to say thank you. Now, phonics. P h o n e means sound or voice. And p h says f! Microphone. Micro means small. A microphone makes small sounds big. Headphones. Smartphone. Xylophone. Xylo means wood. A xylophone makes wooden sounds. Let's practice asking a favor!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Yesterday, Riko asked Birimo to give me a message. Today, let's learn how to pass on a message. Haru says, I am busy. Later, you tell me, He said he was busy. Say it with me. He said he was busy. Wonderful! After said, we often use the past form. Am and is become was. Will becomes would. Kiko says, I will call back. You tell Riko, Kiko called you. She said she would call back later. Riko can answer, Thanks for telling me. Let's read Birimo's message for me. "Ms. Emma, Riko called you at two. She said she had a question about the bird show. She said the paint was ready. Please call her back. From Birimo." Thank you, Birimo! That's a perfect message. Now, phonics. G r a p h means write or draw. Photograph. Photo means light. A photograph is a picture drawn with light! Autograph. Auto means self. An autograph is your name written by yourself. Paragraph. Graphic. Let's pass on messages!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today, let's play a game. It's called Message Relay. We stand in a line. The first person whispers a message. Then each person passes it on. The last person says the message out loud. Is it the same? Let's see! When you pass on a message right now, use says. Riko says the bus leaves at nine. Say it with me. Riko says the bus leaves at nine. Great! Use says for a message you are passing on now. Use said for something a person said before. Let's read the game rules. "Message Relay Rules. One. Listen carefully. Two. Whisper the message to the next person only once. Three. Start with, Riko says. Four. The last person says the message to everyone. Five. Laugh together if it changes!" Sometimes messages change. That's why we check. Did you hear the message right? Now, phonics. P h o t o means light. Photographer. Photocopy. Let's review the other parts, too. Telephone. Tele means far. Autograph. Graph means write. Ready? Let's play!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is a review day. We will work at the Message Center for one whole day. Let's go! In the morning, the phone rings. Hello, Message Center. Can I take a message? In the afternoon, we give the messages to people. Here's a message for you. Say it with me. Here's a message for you. Great! Then tell the message. Ms. Emma called. She said the meeting was at four. The person says, Thank you for the message. Let's read the Message Center diary. "Today was busy! In the morning, Kiko answered ten calls. Haru took five messages. Birimo sorted the letters, but he dropped some. Riko delivered the messages to every floor. In the evening, we were tired, but happy. Our job is important. Messages connect people!" Wonderful. Remember the words from this week. Hold on, please. Could you tell her to call me back? He said he was busy. Now, phonics review. Telephone. Microphone. Autograph. Photographer. Tele, far. Phone, sound. Graph, write. Photo, light. You did a great job today!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Oh no! Something happened in the tower kitchen. Last night, there was a big apple pie on the table. This morning, the pie is gone! Who ate it? Let's ask questions like detectives. We want to know what people were doing last night. We ask, What were you doing at seven? Say it with me. What were you doing at seven? Very good! This is a new form. Was or were, plus i n g. I was reading. You were sleeping. We were washing the dishes. It means the action was happening at that time. Listen. At seven, I was talking on the phone in my room. Let's read Kiko's detective notebook. "The Missing Pie. Last night, the pie was on the kitchen table at six. At eight, it was missing. There were crumbs on the floor. There was a small feather near the window. Question: What was everyone doing at seven?" Hmm, a feather! That's a clue. Now, phonics. M e n t makes a naming word. Agree, agreement. Pay, payment. Move, movement. Keep the e in movement! Detectives watch every movement. Let's find out who ate the pie!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last night at seven, I called Haru. Ring, ring, ring. But he didn't answer. Why? This morning, Haru said, I was taking a bath when you called. Say it with me. I was taking a bath when you called. Great! I was taking a bath is the long action. When you called is the short action. The phone call happened in the middle of the bath. Here's another one. I was brushing my teeth when you called. When someone asks, Why didn't you answer the phone? you can say, Sorry I missed your call. I was taking a bath. Let's read Haru's text message to me. "Hi, Ms. Emma. Sorry I missed your call last night. I was taking a bath when you called. I saw your message after my bath, but it was late. Is it about the missing pie? I didn't eat it! Haru" Ha ha. Okay, Haru. Now, phonics. Excite, excitement. Enjoy, enjoyment. Announce, announcement. Improve, improvement. Keep the e! Excitement has an e before m e n t. Let's practice saying why we missed a call.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Good morning! Look out the window. Everything is white! While we were sleeping, it snowed. Say it with me. While we were sleeping, it snowed. Beautiful! While means during the time. We were sleeping for a long time. During that time, it snowed. You can say it another way, too. It was still snowing when I woke up. Let's read Riko's diary. "This morning, I woke up early. It was very quiet. While I was sleeping, it snowed a lot. The tower was white, and the sky was bright. While I was looking outside, I saw tiny footprints in the snow. They went from the kitchen window to the top of the tower. Whose footprints were they?" Interesting! The footprints are another clue for our pie mystery. Now, phonics. N e s s makes a naming word from a describing word. Kind, kindness. Sad, sadness. Dark, darkness. Bright, brightness. The brightness of the snow hurts my eyes! Let's follow the footprints!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! This morning, something funny happened in the tower kitchen. Riko was cooking pancakes. Then the phone rang. Riko says, When the phone rang, I was cooking. Say it with me. When the phone rang, I was cooking. Great! Rang is the past of ring. Ring, rang. Now listen. While I was talking on the phone, the pancake burned. Oh no! Do you see the difference? When, plus a short action. The phone rang. While, plus a long action. I was talking on the phone. Let's read the story. "This morning, Riko was cooking pancakes with Ms. Emma. When the phone rang, she was flipping a pancake. It was Captain Pip, the head bird of the tower. While Riko was talking on the phone, the pancake burned. Smoke filled the kitchen. Birimo opened the window. When the smoke went out, everyone laughed. Captain Pip said he wanted to tell us something important." Hmm. What does Captain Pip want to say? Remember, always cook with an adult. Now, phonics. Happy, happiness. Lonely, loneliness. Change y to i! Soft, softness. Move, movement. Let's tell our kitchen story!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is the big day. Let's solve the pie mystery! Detectives, let's check our notes. At seven, what was everyone doing? Haru was taking a bath. Riko was writing a letter. Birimo was reading. Kiko was painting. Say it with me. Birimo was reading. Kiko was painting. Good! So they didn't eat the pie. Then who did? Remember the clues. A small feather. Tiny footprints in the snow. Crumbs on the stairs. Let's read the last page of Kiko's detective notebook. "We followed the footprints to the top of the tower. There was a nest. In the nest, there were three baby birds and Captain Pip. Their faces were covered with apple pie! Captain Pip looked sad. He said, I'm sorry. My babies were hungry." So it was a hungry little bird! Captain Pip wanted to tell us on the phone. We said, That's okay. Let's bake another pie together. That was real kindness. Now, phonics review. Agreement. Excitement. Kindness. Happiness. What a happy ending! Now, present your mystery story!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! I'm talking to you from the basement of the tower. There are many old books here, so I'm staying for a few days. Please send me emails from the tower study! An email has three parts. First, the greeting. Dear Ms. Emma, How are you? Say it with me. Dear Ms. Emma, How are you? Lovely! Second, the main message. Why are you writing? Today, I want to tell you about the snow. Third, the ending. Please write back soon. And don't forget the subject. The subject tells the main idea in a few words. Let's read Kiko's email. "Subject: Snow at the Tower. Dear Ms. Emma, How are you? Today, I want to tell you about the snow. While we were sleeping, it snowed a lot. We made a snow bird on the roof. Captain Pip liked it! Please write back soon. From Kiko" Wonderful! Greeting, message, ending. Now, phonics. Today, we listen to linking sounds. When one word ends with a consonant and the next word starts with a vowel, they connect. Hold on. Can I. Come in. Can I come in? Let's write an email!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! I got Kiko's email. Thank you, Kiko! Now I'll write back. When you answer an email, start with, Thanks for your email. I was happy to hear from you. Say it with me. Thanks for your email. I was happy to hear from you. Excellent! Hear from you means get a message from you. Then answer the news. That sounds like fun! And you can ask a question. I have a question for you. Asking a question is good. Then your friend will write back again. Let's read my reply. "Subject: Re: Snow at the Tower. Dear Kiko, Thanks for your email. I was happy to hear from you. A snow bird on the roof? That sounds like fun! Here in the basement, I found a very old book about an amber library. I have a question for you. What are you going to do this week? Best wishes, Ms. Emma" Look at the subject. R e means it's a reply. Now, phonics. Check it out. Pick it up. Think about it. Check it out! There's a new email for you. Let's write a reply!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! How do you end an email? Today, let's choose closing words. For a friend, you can write, See you soon. Best wishes, Riko. Say it with me. See you soon. Best wishes, Riko. Great! Best wishes is good for teachers, friends, and almost everyone. For close family or best friends, you can write, Love, Kiko. For a friend you will talk to again, write, Take care. Talk to you later. Put your name or nickname on the next line. Let's read three endings. Who is each one for? "One. See you on Monday. Best wishes, Haru. Two. Take care, Grandma! Love, Riko. Three. Thank you for your help. Best wishes, Kiko." Number one is for a classmate. Number two is for Grandma. Number three is for a teacher. Good! Now, phonics. Leave a message. Take a message. Send it. An email. Listen again. Leave a. Take a. Send it. An email. Can you write an email and send it today? Let's choose endings!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The internet is useful and fun. We can send emails and make video calls. But we need to be careful. Today, let's talk about internet safety. Rule number one. Don't share your address online. Say it with me. Don't share your address online. Very good! Don't share your phone number, your school name, or your photos with strangers, either. Rule number two. Keep your password secret. Only your family can know it. Rule number three. If something feels strange, tell an adult. Let's read the tower's poster. "Stay Safe Online! Use a nickname. Never meet an online friend alone. Don't click strange links. Log in only on safe sites. Be kind in your messages. If something feels strange, turn off the screen and tell an adult." These rules are very important. You are not in trouble when you tell an adult. Now, phonics. Log in. Sign in. Turn on. Turn off. Can you hear the links? Let's talk about safety together.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! The tower has a pen pal program. You can exchange emails with children in faraway countries. Today, Haru got an email from a pen pal called Leo. Leo is a nickname. That's safe! Now, Haru is writing back. To start the main message, he writes, I'm writing to tell you about my trip. Say it with me. I'm writing to tell you about my trip. Great! Then use linking words. First. Then. Also. Let's read Haru's email. "Subject: Hello from the Tower! Dear Leo, Thanks for your email. I was happy to hear from you. I'm writing to tell you about my trip. First, we visited a festival on an island. Then, we came to a tall tower. Birds carry letters here. Also, we solved a pie mystery! What's your town like? Please write back soon. Best wishes, Haru" Look. A greeting. A main message with First, Then, and Also. A question. A closing. Perfect! He didn't write his address or his school. Good! Now, phonics review. Hold on. Check it out. Take a message. Log in. Let's write to a pen pal!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! In messages, we often use emojis. Emojis are small pictures. But sometimes we don't know what they mean. Today, let's explain emojis in English. Look at this one. This emoji means "I'm excited." Say it with me. This emoji means "I'm excited." Wonderful! When you explain something, you can say, It looks like a face with big, shiny eyes. You can use it when you're happy about something. Let's read Kiko's emoji dictionary. "The crying-laughing face. It looks like a face with tears. But it doesn't mean sad. It means something is very funny. The thumbs-up. It means okay, or good job. The sleepy face. You can use it when you're tired." Be careful! In different countries, some emojis mean different things. If you're not sure, ask. And don't use only emojis. Emojis make messages fun, but words are clearer. Now, phonics review. Dislike. Mistake. Preview. Enjoyment. Which word parts do you see? Dis, mis, pre, and ment. Let's talk about emojis!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We learned three ways to connect: phone calls, video calls, and emails. Which way is the best? It depends! Today, let's compare them and give our opinions. Listen. I think email is better for long messages. Say it with me. I think email is better for long messages. Great! Why? Because you can read it again later. A phone call is faster than an email. I like video calls because I can see my friend's face. Let's read what our friends said. "Haru: I think phone calls are better for quick questions. They're fast. Riko: I like video calls because I can see my grandma's smile. Kiko: I think email is better for long messages. I can think carefully before I send it. Birimo: I like letters by bird post! They're slow, but exciting!" Everyone has a different opinion, and that's okay. When you give an opinion, say a reason with because. Now, phonics review. Telephone. Autograph. Kindness. Hold on. Which way do you like? Let's share our opinions!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Captain Pip has a present for us. He says, My birds can take your letters to your families. How nice! Today, let's write a letter by bird post. Start like this. I'm writing this letter from the top of the tower. Say it with me. I'm writing this letter from the top of the tower. Lovely! Then share your feelings. I miss you, but I'm having a great time. Then tell your news. And when you give the letter to the bird, ask politely. Could you take this letter to my family? Let's read Riko's letter. "Dear Mom and Dad, How are you? I'm writing this letter from the top of the tower. I miss you, but I'm having a great time. Last week, we solved a pie mystery. I was writing a letter when the pie disappeared! It was a hungry bird. Also, it snowed! Please say hello to Grandma. Love, Riko" Isn't it warm? Letters have the same parts as emails. Now, phonics review. Disagree. Photographer. Excitement. Check it out. Let's write our letters!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Tomorrow is our last day in the Tower of Messages. Today, let's take a goodbye tour of the tower and remember what we learned. First, the phone room. May I speak to Captain Pip, please? Say it with me. May I speak to Captain Pip, please? Great! Hold on, please. I'll get him. Next, the video call room. Can you hear me? You're on mute. The screen froze. Can you say that again? Then, the Message Center. Can I take a message? He said he was busy. Next, the kitchen. Do you remember the pie mystery? What were you doing at seven? I was taking a bath when you called. While we were sleeping, it snowed. Finally, the study. Dear Ms. Emma, How are you? Best wishes. Let's read the tower guide. "Tower of Messages Guide. Second floor: phone room. Third floor: video call room. Fifth floor: Message Center. Sixth floor: kitchen. Seventh floor: study. Top floor: radio station." A radio station? Tomorrow, we will go there! Now, phonics review. Disconnect. Misunderstand. Microphone. Happiness. Can I. Let's start the tour!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Welcome to the World 21 Grand Review! We're at the top of the tower, in the radio station. Today, we will make a radio program called Tower Radio. People will call in, and we will answer. At the end of each call, we say, Thank you for calling. Talk to you soon! Say it with me. Thank you for calling. Talk to you soon! Fantastic! In this world, you learned so much. Hello, this is Haru. May I speak to Riko? Hold on, please. Can you hear me? You're on mute. The screen froze. Can you say that again? Can I take a message? He said he was busy. What were you doing at seven? I was taking a bath when you called. While we were sleeping, it snowed. Dear Ms. Emma. Best wishes. Don't share your address online. Here is our program plan. Let's read it. "Tower Radio. Part one: News from the tower. Part two: Calls from listeners. Part three: A song by the bird singer. Part four: A goodbye message." Now, phonics review. Disappear. Preview. Telephone. Agreement. Hold on. You are great communicators. Let's go on the air!
